purpose: Primary-source review for adaptive Cantonese IME personalization and compact candidate UI. This records design choices, not evidence that all techniques below have been implemented.

observed_techniques: Commit processing can collect selected phrase components into a user phrase.
User entries retain spelling codes, selected text, commit counts and a usage tick.
Dynamic entry scoring incorporates frequency and decayed usage; user-dictionary search distinguishes exact and predictive matches.
Recent transactions can be reverted rather than permanently teaching every mistaken commit.
User-history scoring uses last access with candidate-length and bigram adjustments.
Matching distinguishes exact input, shorter prefixes and longer input requiring linked history entries.
Neighboring history entries support phrase chaining and contextual suggestions.
Low-frequency whole-sentence suggestions can be suppressed in the relevant mixed-conversion mode.
Personal history scores both individual words and preceding-word/current-word pairs, with optional spelling validation codes.
History uses several bounded recency pools with different weights.
The user language model blends history scores with the static language model.

project_design_inferences: Keep preferences conditional on complete normalized input and spelling mode. A learned long phrase must not automatically take over every shorter prefix.
Use adaptive competing-choice weights rather than a permanent single mapping or unbounded lifetime-count advantage.
Retain validly selected whole phrases in a local personal phrase store, including composed candidates, so bounded static search does not later hide them.
Learn only after successful candidate commit; cancel, literal Latin, lookup and failed commits must not teach the model.
Keep learning transport off the TSF edit thread, preserve commit order, and save bounded per-user state atomically across sessions.

Preceding-word context, new phrases assembled across separate commits, correction/revert feedback and a trained Cantonese language model are further extensions; the initial adaptive full-input model does not claim them.

initial_policy.decay_scope: Same full normalized input and mode only; shorter and longer inputs remain independent.
initial_policy.policy_status: Project-authored heuristic to verify with regression cases and user examples; not copied from an upstream probability model.

ui_design.contents: Candidate words only; no duplicate phonetic header, readings, numeric labels or instructional footer.
ui_design.layout: Measured horizontal cells that wrap within a bounded, DPI-aware popup; highlight and existing selection/paging keys remain.
